hypothesis: The RPC stdio surface (PR #2801 stub S5; crates/pa-daemon/src/rpc/ + the pa-cli --mode rpc entry) has zero fleet perf numbers. Its create/resume flows ride the same engine seams the staged lanes own (the in-process pa-core create_session equivalents of the daemon facade's ensure_core_session->build_session->adopt_built_session), so the file-pass/lock-cycle findings apply there too; the baseline decomposes its cold-open/resume/create cost classes per fixture shape, the durable writes per RPC command, and the lock cycles per fresh RPC session (do the #2932/#2941 auth+settings consolidations apply on this path?), and compares each class against the TUI->daemon->worker equivalent on the same VM — the delta is the surface's own cost.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY, no product change (baseline lane; the record is the deliverable). Pinned tip 4df41f66a (HEAD churn during the lane: #2744 runtime/kernel hardening, #2763 daemon-restart wait, #2942/#2943 test/pa-tui-only — all off rpc/ or comment-only vs my territory; the baseline pins the build). VM r9bfra2rhhe1m4a53dy5g2bk (hillclimb-perf-rpc-baseline, ubuntu:22.04 16c/32GB/100GB, rustup 1.98.1), cargo build --release --locked --workspace rc=0, binary sha ad74c51e05a15a561a3f3c16c1dc6b16d2c30e4c1d63089248d4a22babc20abe (221974544 bytes). Bench harness deployed on the VM (product.yaml binary+revision pinned to the VM build; settle OK; kernel venv warm at bench/global/rust). Fixtures rebuilt on-VM, shas matching the fleet-known values: session-10mib-compacted 97beb5eb... (rows 10984, retained 105047B, firstKeptEntryId 00002a61), stock session-10mib dadaecfc... (7391 rows). REAL assembly path, offline mock provider (prime-inference/mock-1 via models.json + bench mock_provider, the spawn-latency lane contract; zero network inference). Driver: rpc_probe.py (per-trial fresh agent dir/home/tmp/cwd; scrubbed env + venv-env.json; per-trial fixture prehash assert on resume; loadavg quiet gate; product-only zombie sweep; nonblocking os.read frame pump, 10ms windows + per-window response match; per-command wall receipts). Legs (same-VM sequential, A-B-B-A interleave per class, binary sha asserted per block, I/O advisory v1.0 preflights before every block + pre/post): FRESH: A=compare.cold_start harness TUI legs x8 vs B=--mode rpc fresh x8; RESUME: A=session.cold_open_10mib_compacted x8 (sentinel-validated) vs B=--mode rpc --resume compacted-fixture x8; STOCK: A=session.cold_open_10mib x8 vs B=--mode rpc --resume stock-fixture x8; NO-SESSION attribution leg x6; CENSUS x5 (strace -ff -f -tt, structure-only, INVALID for timing): 3x fresh first-turn + 2x resume; lock census via the settings-lane parser pattern (mkdir/rmdir pairs on *.lock dirs, 20ms clock_nanosleep retries, same-process racing pairs) + per-command durable-write windows anchored to the strace time-of-day; TUI-equivalent legs are the gold-standard harness suites (their historical comparators; probe grid 0.5s/2ms disclosed).
parity_notes: No product source changed in any phase; frozen parity untouched (no session-JSONL/wire/prompt/TUI bytes touched; the RPC surface was only exercised as a black box over its own stdio). The engine seams owned by the staged lanes (agent_engine.rs/model.rs/create.rs) were measurement-only territory. The bench harness + mock provider are offline verification harnesses, not product. Two harness-behavior artifacts were found and fixed during the campaign, both MINE, both disclosed: (1) the driver's first read loop parked parsed frames behind a full 60s pump window (a false '60s per command stall' — the bisection harness proved the surface answers in 50-250ms; the product was never at fault); (2) a 0.2s pump-window quantization inflated every per-command wall by up to +200ms and the ready walls similarly (fixed to 10ms windows; all timing legs re-run after the fix — the numbers below are the corrected re-run).

The TUI arm's numbers are the gold-standard harness suites with their 0.5s/2ms probe grids — the arms' measurement contracts differ (the RPC side is arrival-accurate to 10ms; the harness side is its historical contract), so the deltas are structural and one-directional, not a like-for-like paired microsecond comparison. decision: Baseline delivered: the RPC surface's cost map is decomposed per class, the TUI-equivalent deltas measured on the same VM, the lock census answers the consolidation question (YES — 0 per-turn cycles; the cost is per-connection/per-replacement), the durable-write census maps every command, and the candidates are reported-only for the orchestrator's queue. The surface is CHEAP: 21ms fresh cold-open, 135-187ms resume of 10MiB fixtures, 25ms warm replacements, 31ms EOF settle — and structurally cheaper than the TUI->daemon->worker path on every fixture class (the stock/no-boundary class by 4.2x).
